compactRecord.rs: Encountering Japan's oldest living being after an all-day pilgrimage through cloud forest is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
compactRecord.td: Giant Yaku-sugi cedar (Cryptomeria japonica) at 1,300 m on the slopes of Mt Miyanoura, 25.3 m tall and 16.4 m girth; tree-ring dating suggests 2,000–7,000 years old. Reached via 22 km round-trip Arakawa Trail along disused Kosugidani forestry railway

compactRecord.rs: One of the only Ramsar-listed turtle-nesting beaches you can join guided night patrols on (mid-May to mid-Aug).
compactRecord.td: 800 m crescent of white granite-sand beach on Yakushima's northwest coast, registered Ramsar wetland (2005). Japan's most important loggerhead sea-turtle nesting site — 5,000+ hatchlings emerge July–August. Sunset views to Kuchinoerabu-jima volcano.
